evidence:
WHAT HOLDS: tests/scoring.toml and tests/tools/score.py are byte-identical to the template (diff clean): gates render/constraints = 0.0 with all_pass; weights functional 0.6, polish 0.2, visual 0.2; floor functional 0.05. score.py:41-48 sets reward to the weighted mean only when every gate score is > 0 and functional is > 0.05, so reward rises monotonically with each dimension score. Function outweighs craft (0.6 against 0.4 combined), and no gate carries reward mass. Per-criterion weights follow one documented scheme ('Criterion weights: 1.0 standard, 1.5 important, 2.0 core'). Functional has 44 binary criteria totalling 61.0, polish 5 totalling 9.5, and visual 5 equal-weight likert rows. A weighted_mean of binary rows is monotone in the set of passed rows. Dead features earn no credit: every refusal row names a same-kind positive control (e.g. hro_reject_hired, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_undo_once, hro_undo_full, hro_mgr_other_job), and functional/prompt.md:13 says 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'. The role rows (hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous) leave out request kinds whose staff control never succeeded and score 0 if none succeeded. A broken app gains nothing there, and a stronger app is not penalised twice. The gates test only public, basic requirements and accept another staff account, so a stronger conforming app should not fail them. Render checks that a wrong password is refused and the right one signs in. Constraints adds a candidate through the UI, reloads, and has the Observer find it in an independent context (hireops_rules.md section 2 'A recruiter adds a candidate...'; section 1 Observer 'reads the board'). Polish/prompt.md:11-12 and visual/prompt.md:11-12 repeat the same check inside their dimensions, so a non-working shell cannot farm craft points. Some cascades already have fallbacks: functional/prompt.md:47 switches to Tomas's seeded Data Analyst conversation if the linked card never appears, and :49 lets Mei Lin send if Tomas cannot.
DEFECT (cascade inversion): job opening has no fallback, and nearly the whole board suite depends on it. functional/prompt.md:13 allows re-setup only 'on a new job of your own if that is possible without the broken feature', and :15 says 'Use your own new jobs and cards for every board protocol'. Protocol S (:35) opens J1 (Ingrid, 2 places) and J2 (Bill, 2 places), and protocols M, L, C, B, N, R, V and A (:37-57) all run on J1/J2. polish hro_pol_live_board says 'add cards to your job', and polish/prompt.md:14 says 'Use your own new job and cards'. A single weight-1 defect in hro_job_open therefore leaves the judge no permitted way to run those protocols. About 45 of the 61 functional weight units then go to 0: every M/L/C/B/R/N/V/A row, the other-job control in hro_add_email_rules, and the job legs of hro_restart. The 2.0 polish live-board row goes with them. The seeded Data Analyst job (2 places) could stand in, but the prompt never allows it. The lessons file (items 15, 16 and 18) and REVIEW_POLICY ('Independent credit takes precedence over flow grouping'; 'Preserve valid observations rather than inheriting a sibling verdict') warn against this pattern. I checked every protocol for other unprotected upstream setups. A2 from the email-rules leg can be rebuilt under the generic re-setup clause (a new J2 card with a fresh email). The Tomas link and send have explicit fallbacks. Add-candidate sits behind the gate, which is all-or-nothing by template design (see note b). Job opening is the only unprotected one.
MISSING MEASUREMENT: the scope field of raw-evidence-index.json says 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'. Its only entries are the scripted golden driver (26 groups). REVIEW_POLICY requires hash-bound reward-ordering and discrimination records before clearance, and no ranking of mutated weak apps has been measured. A second ranking risk is also unmeasured. test.sh runs the suites one at a time (--max-concurrent-agent 1) with a scored budget of 11100 s, against judge timeouts of functional 9000 + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10800 s. A strong app makes the judge walk every protocol leg, including many 15 s timed observations, while a broken app ends legs early. If the functional judge runs out of time on a strong app, the prompt's NOT EXERCISED rule scores the unobserved rows 0. If rewardkit itself fails, the run_suite failure branch exits with the gate-stage record (reward 0). Either way a better app can score below a worse one, and no full configured judge duration exists to rule this out.
NOTES (not defects for this row): (a) The template fixes the 0.6/0.2/0.2 split and the 0.05 floor (3.05 of 61 weight units). An extreme visual difference can therefore reorder two apps whose functional scores are close. That is template policy, not a task choice, and it must not change. (b) The gate makes reward all-or-nothing on UI add-candidate. That is a core public requirement and the template's intended gate shape (lesson 4: load, reload, server-backed). (c) A live-update failure costs both functional rows (hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, unread, seen) and polish rows (pol_live_board and pol_live_thread are 0 if no update arrives). That is a double-penalty question for row 28 and does not invert the order between a live and a non-live app.
counterexample: App S (better) gets every board rule right: one-stage moves, order, reject/reopen, interview places, put-back with focus, a stale 409 naming the mover, all-or-none bulk moves, undo and its conflicts, roles, activity and the live board. Its conversations are also correct. But its New job form always fails, for example because the hiring-manager select posts the display name and the server answers 400, so hro_job_open = 0. Both gates pass because they use the seeded Data Analyst job. Under functional/prompt.md:13/:15 the judge cannot create J1/J2 and may not substitute a seeded job. Every M/L/C/B/R/N/V/A row and polish hro_pol_live_board are therefore 0. Functional comes to about (1 add_candidate plus conversation and candidate rows: msg_exchange 1.5, msg_compose 1, thread_latest 1.5, thread_earlier 2, unread 2, scrolled_up 2, seen 1.5, drafts 2, candidate_view 1.5, candidate_private 2, linked 1, restart 1.5) / 61, roughly 0.33. App W (worse): job opening and add-candidate work, but a server bug refuses every stage move and nothing else on the board works. Its conversations are as correct as S's. W earns hro_job_open 1, hro_add_candidate 1, hro_add_email_rules 1 and hro_notes 1 on top of the same conversation rows. It can also earn the hro_pol_live_board legs once a card is added. So W >= S on functional and polish while implementing far fewer of the brief's rules.
suggested_fix: In functional/prompt.md, and in the polish board row, add an explicit fallback: if opening a job fails (graded only in hro_job_open), run the board protocols on the seeded Data Analyst job (2 places, its own hiring manager) with your own suffixed cards, use that job's manager wherever J1/J2 name Ingrid or Bill, and score each row from what you observe. Then collect hash-bound reward-ordering and discrimination evidence on mutated weak apps, plus a full configured functional-judge duration on the golden.
